_README: Cited joint-rule table (doc 16 §2 Source C/D, doc 13 rules engine). Rafix-type eccentric shelf connector — the heavy/secured F3_shelf_adjustable alternate per catalog/CORE_DOCTRINE.md ('rafix-type eccentric (MM-FI20) for heavy/secured'). Cross-brand equivalent group: GTV's MM-FI20 and Hettich's VB 35/36 share the same function_group and, per the sources below, essentially the same housing diameter — the doc17 R4 substitutability claim is directly supported here, not just asserted.

sources.scope: 'shelf_eccentric_rafix_type' entry in catalog/packs/gtv_2025_06/connectors_pilot.json — MM-FI20 SKU family (MM-FI20-20X6X11-PL10/20/30/80-1T, -ZN-1T), housing Ø20mm (from SKU), dowel Ø6×16.5mm, seat depths seen in drawing: 11.5/12.5/13.5mm (already flagged in-source as needing visual re-confirmation, drawing dims interleaved with text).

VB 35/36 connecting fittings: housing Ø20mm, depth ~9.5mm, screw-in dowel Ø5mm (this document's own figure; note it differs from GTV's Ø6mm dowel — see gap below); VB35 M/19 dowel centre 14mm from the shelf underside on a 19mm shelf; VB36 M is 'pressed into a double hole drilled 32mm apart, insertion holes in a diameter of 20 and 10mm'.
het_vb35 accessory (catalog/packs/core_2026_06/accessories/het_vb35.json) — full technical section, browse-grade only, pages known but not transcribed to numbers here.

bands.dowel_diameter_mm: 6 (GTV) vs 5 (Hettich 2016 flyer) — UNRESOLVED conflict, see gap_flag
bands.confidence: housing diameter (Ø20) independently confirmed by both brands and by 2/2 mined rafix_20 instances — the strongest cross-brand agreement of any figure in this file. Every other number here is single-source or conflicting.

gap_flag: Dowel diameter conflict: GTV's connectors_pilot.json states the rafix dowel is Ø6mm; the Hettich 2016 flyer states VB35/36's screw-in dowel is Ø5mm. These may legitimately be different-diameter dowels for the same Ø20 housing across brands (plausible, since R4 only requires the DRILLED housing to be substitution-compatible, not every internal dowel), or one of the two transcriptions is wrong. Do not merge into a single verified number without checking a rendered page of each source side by side.
placement_principles_from_source: Hettich VB 36 M: 'pressed into a double hole drilled 32mm apart, insertion holes in a diameter of 20 and 10mm' — i.e. TWO different-diameter holes per fitting (Ø20 housing + Ø10 secondary), 32mm apart. GTV's MM-FI20 SKU naming (20X6X11) does not obviously encode a second hole diameter — worth checking whether GTV's version is single-hole or also double-hole; not resolved here.
No minimum shelf-edge distance or load-per-fitting figure located in either source on hand.

mined_cross_check.evidence_text: 'Ø20 face seat (first sighting — none seen before)' — the extractor's own language flags this as a novel, low-confidence detection, not an established pattern.
mined_cross_check.verdict: Weakest mined evidence of all seven families by row count (2 rows total, both from the same project). The 17mm depth class does not match either brand's housing-depth figures above (GTV 11.5-13.5mm, Hettich ~9.5mm) — another unresolved gap, possibly because a 17mm-deep Ø20 bore is a DIFFERENT feature (e.g. a lift or hinge seat, cf. hinge_cup's own Ø35 face bore at 13mm depth, or gtv_hinge_glass's Ø20-class hardware) that the extractor is currently mis-bucketing into 'rafix_20' rather than a real rafix sighting.

engine_notes: This is the family with the most open questions of the seven researched here: a cross-brand dowel-diameter conflict, a depth mismatch between the mined data and both catalogued sources, and only 2 mined rows to cross-check against — well below doc 16's ≥95%-agreement replay bar and too thin to draw any conclusion from. Before any use in the solver: (1) render GTV p.271 and Hettich pp.745/748-751 directly rather than relying on the pilot transcription and a 2016 flyer; (2) ask the constructor (doc 16 §2 Source B) whether the 2 mined Ø20×17mm sightings are actually rafix fittings or something else, since the extractor itself flagged them as novel/unconfident.
replay_evidence_R43: DB/37_JOINT_SELECTION_RULES.md §4 replayed a held-out real cabinet (a shelf_unit with no rafix-class hardware expected) and found ZERO Ø20-class holes — consistent with absence, but this is not a positive test of the family; it still has only the original 2 corpus rows behind it. Still the weakest-evidence family; needs a held-out cabinet that actually uses rafix/VB-type shelf connectors before this rule can be exercised at all.
